name: SACH foot
description: Staros (VA), 1957. Wood keel, rubber shell, compressible foam heel, "standard due to its availability, inexpensiveness, and durability."

name: Single-axis foot
description: Hinged ankle with rubber bumper (e.g., Otto Bock).

name: Jaipur foot
description: Sethi, 1970s, India. Second most used prosthesis after SACH: hundreds of thousands of users across 20+ countries.

name: Wood exoskeletal shank
description: Laminated wood/plastic lower leg. Period-standard component.

name: Leather corset socket
description: Lacer leather socket suspension. Period-standard component.

name: Jaipur foot
description: Still widely used in low-resource settings.

name: Carbon-fiber energy-storing foot
description: Composite laminates; the ESAR class arrives in the late 1980s.

name: Microprocessor foot
description: Össur Proprio, "the world's first bionic prosthetic foot," launched mid-2006.

name: Powered foot
description: BiOM (~2013–14), Ottobock Empower (>1,500 in use). No metabolic claim is made for powered feet.
